lesson.subtitle: Lesson 10 -- Understood, Not Perfect
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fernanda Bassani Rubio | Lesson 10 -- Understood, Not Perfect
lesson.grammar_point: present perfect for experience with ever and never

listenings.text: Hello, Fernanda. You asked me about my English. Well, I have worked in this company for eleven years, and I have worked with people from about twenty countries. I have never spoken perfect English. I know I have an accent, and I know I speak fast when I am tired. But I have learned one important thing: people do not need perfect English. They need to understand each other. When you asked me to repeat, or to write something in the chat, it helped me too. So thank you. Your English has improved a lot this year.

You know, Fernanda, I have tried to learn Portuguese. Two times, actually. I have used apps, and I have watched Brazilian series with subtitles. But I have never given a presentation in Portuguese. I can say only three sentences: good morning, thank you, and see you later. So when you present to us in English, I think about that. You are working in your second language, and you are doing it well. I respect that a lot.

to become comfortable with something new

paras: Have you ever been on a global call with people from five countries? Then you know this: most people who speak English at work are not native speakers. They are from China, India, Germany, Brazil, France and many other places. Everybody has an accent, and everybody makes mistakes. The calls work anyway.

Many professionals say the same thing. At first, the accents were difficult. But after some weeks, they got used to them. They learned simple tools: ask the person to repeat, ask for names and numbers in the chat, and confirm the important points at the end. Their listening improved, and they felt more confident.

What do managers value in a meeting? Not perfect grammar. They value clear ideas, good questions and a clear recommendation. You do not need to be fluent to lead a good meeting. You need to be clear. So, if you have ever stayed quiet on a call because of your English, remember: the other people on the call are not native speakers either. They are just like you.
reading.source: Alumni by Better -- A2 reading, written for this lesson from common experience in global teams
